name: Shredded Chicken Tacos with Pico and Cilantro-Lime Rice
description: Taco Tuesday built on Monday's leftover chicken thighs — shredded, crisped in a skillet with warm spices, and piled into street tortillas with fresh pico.
ingredients: 2–3 cooked chicken thighs, meat shredded and skin discarded (about 2 cups)
Sour cream or crema, for serving
instructions: Start the rice: combine rice, water, and a big pinch of salt in a saucepan. Boil, cover, drop to low, cook 18 minutes, then rest covered 5 minutes off the heat.
Make the pico while the rice cooks: toss the tomatoes, white onion, jalapeño, half the cilantro, the juice of 1 lime, and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl. Let it sit — it gets better over 20 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high. Add the shredded chicken in an even layer and leave it alone for 2 minutes so the bottom crisps.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and paprika. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the broth and cook until it's mostly absorbed, about 3 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the extra 1/2 tsp cumin and a splash of their liquid.
Fluff the rice with the remaining cilantro and the juice of 1 lime.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas burner or in a dry skillet, about 20 seconds a side. Stack them in a clean towel to stay warm.
Build: chicken, pico, cheese, crema, and a squeeze from the last lime.
tips: The splash of broth is what keeps reheated chicken from going dry — don't skip it and don't let it fully evaporate.
Pico needs salt and time more than it needs anything else. Salt it first, then leave it.
Two tortillas per taco is the street-taco standard and it's not just tradition — one tortilla tears under the crema.
